newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU likely to agree farm animal welfare rules.
newsitem.headline: EU likely to agree farm animal welfare rules.

text.p: European Union farm ministers may on Tuesday reach political agreement on rules to improve farm animal welfare during long distance journeys, EU diplomats said.
Final agreement on minimum standards for animal rest centres, feeding, watering, loading, unloading and animal health requirements is only possible after the European Parliament has given an opinion.
"Most technical points have been fixed," said one diplomat.

The rest centres were agreed as part of a deal reached by farm ministers in June 1995 after five years of heated talks on ways to protect animals during long journeys to slaughter. The deal should have entered into force at the end of 1996 but has still not been applied.
Cattle, pigs, sheep and other farm animals are entitled to a 24-hour rest after travelling for a minimum eight hours and before continuing their journeys.
Italy has requested EU aid to help equip the centres but the European Commission believes the cost should be borne by industry.
Disagreement over the start-up date of the new measures still has to be resolved with July 1998 and November 1999 the dates proposed.

Britain, backed by Denmark, has requested special treatment for high value breeding pigs. Officials said that the pigs are transported in luxury vehicles and do not need to be unloaded at rest centres. It could also put them at risk to disease.
